title: Request storm mitigation and KV-eviction stabilizer for customer escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-volume tenant migration on 2026-03-09 we observed a customer-visible cascade of 5xx errors and timeouts originating from retry amplification. The root trigger was an orchestration of many small clients simultaneously reissuing requests after transient timeouts; that amplified load produced oversized batching and frequent KV cache churn which caused worker memory pressure and intermittent OOM/restart behavior in the serving runtime. Impact: several customers experienced elevated error rates and long tail latency for ~3 hours; some enterprise tenants reported production disruption and opened escalations. Scope: hosted API (edge proxy + request router + serving fleet), observable across multiple regions. Goal: ship a short-term mitigation that (1) stops retry amplification and connection fanout, (2) stabilizes KV cache eviction behavior to avoid worker OOMs, and (3) put safe rollout controls (canary + tenant quarantine) to avoid further customer pain.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Initial triage: Ops detected a spike in worker restarts correlated with increased backpressure on the batcher. Tracing shows many clients retried with short backoff windows. Opening ENG-754321 to coordinate hotfix across proxy, router, and runtime teams. Assigned Marco.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Hot mitigation plan approved: (A) apply per-tenant retry suppression at edge (short-circuit retries for tenants with >X errors in Y sec), (B) temporarily lower max batch window (reduce oversized batches), (C) switch KV eviction policy to 'pinned-first' for active prefixes to reduce churn, (D) prevent autoscale burst launches for affected host pools. Ops to implement A and D first as they are config-only and reversible.

2026-03-10 14:27 - Edge change deployed to canary (region: us-west-2): per-tenant retry-suppression active. Observed immediate reduction in fanout and a 45% drop in 5xx rate for canary tenants. No regression in normal traffic in canary.

2026-03-10 16:50 - Runtime hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3891 - adds eviction stabilizer that biases against evicting pinned prefix entries under sustained batch pressure. Unit tests and integration harness added. Requesting review from @sue-jenkins and @li-chen.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Review feedback: li-chen - please add a metrics counter for "eviction-rescue" events and ensure it is exposed to Console. sue-jenkins - small nit on config naming but ok to merge after metrics is added.

2026-03-11 12:40 - Metrics added and PR merged. Staging run (nightly) showed stable memory usage and no OOMs across 24h synthetic tenant storm test. Link to staging run: https://buildkite.redwood-inference.com/builds/10312

2026-03-11 15:15 - Canary rollout for runtime change started in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 limited to non-critical tenants. Monitoring: memory headroom improved, 5xx rate decreased by ~60% for canary targets, tail latency improved. No service-level regression observed.

2026-03-12 08:03 - Customer comms: Support drafted and sent interim update to escalated customers acknowledging root cause and mitigation steps; offered assisted migration window if needed. Ops is keeping retry suppression rules in place for affected tenants until full regression-proof rollout.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Follow-up items noted: add end-to-end test covering simultaneous client reconnect + retry pattern, formalize tenant quarantine policy and SDK guidance to avoid tight reattempt loops, add throttling knob to SDK examples. PRs for follow-ups created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/214
